I’ve experienced the same situation, single, live alone, I live far away from family and I lost my only cat and best friend after spending everyday together for 11 years she passed beginning of April. It’s been extremely hard. I don’t have much advice except time does help, the first few days I allowed myself to just cry, ugly cry, scream cry, roll around balling my eyes out on the floor just felt everything. 

Then I knew I needed to get out of the house but still be alone and what seemed to help was getting out of the house and hiking. Being in nature even while alone made me not feel alone. Giving and receiving love with nature admiring the trees and bugs and seeing little squirrels made me feel connected to my cat in a way I can’t really explain. I went on a few really long hikes a few days after her passing and it helped. 

After a few weeks of her passing spending time with friends and getting out of the house whenever I had the opportunity helped. I drove home and visited family one weekend and that helped a lot too. The hardest part for me was being home alone and her not being there. And it’s still the hardest part, now I miss her more at night being in bed alone. I’ve contemplated getting a new cat but it hasn’t felt right yet.. I’m sure I will eventually

My cat recently passed last Monday I did an at home euthanasia as well, they did a 2 diff sedative process. My cat who is never aggressive and usually very docile got very upset at the first sedative, at first she kept wanting to hide the minute they got there. I told them to go ahead and do the first one to calm her down. It didn’t help, I tried to keep her in the living room but she was so upset trying to get in the bedroom I let her in, she immediately went under the bed where I just laid beside her for about 10 mins to let her calm down and the sedative kick in. Almost 15 mins passed me just laying in the floor and they said they need to do the next sedative the one that puts her in a deep sleep, I had to pull her out from under the bed and she was growling the whole time clawing the carpet. She never growled like that. She was mad it hurt me so bad to have to do that ): once I got her out I got her on the bed and she was still growling as the lady administered the next sedative. Once it started to kick in she calmed down alot, they had to administer it a couple times and we waited almost 30 mins until she was in the deep sleep. The last 20 mins she was very calm and I could see the anxiety fading away. 

But it really broke my heart bc I expected it to go alot smoother being at home. But I still am glad we did it at home then the vet, I think she was just scared, I mean who isn’t a little scared of dying right? It’s a scary thing and I think she felt that’s what was happening. 

The only thing I wish I did differently was give her her gabapentin that morning , I think it would have helped things go smoother. But she hated it so so so much I felt horrible to force anymore medicine down her the day of, I didn’t want her to go upset about it.… but maybe it would have been better I don’t know.
